l1_line1: Vasseur, my right wing. Not that close — I'm fond of my wingtips.
l1_line3: And hands light on her. It's a horse's mouth — pull at it and she pulls back at you.
l1_line4: I've never been on a horse.
l1_line5: No. Well. Take my word for it and we'll say no more about it. We run the line west to east and we don't turn back down it — and if they cut you about badly, the field drops a crate on the line under a parachute. Fly straight through it. Don't go round for a second look, I've watched a man do that.
l1_line6: Chardon 118, nothing reported in the sector since four this morning. Wind westerly, ten. Have him back for lunch, Auguste.
l1_line7: Lunch is ambitious, Henri. And nothing reported isn't the same as nothing there.
l1_line8: Two ahead of us. One behind the other.
l1_line9: There we are, then. They're yours, one at a time — I'll be busy with a third.
l1_line11: I'm giving them to you. It's not the same thing, and you'll feel the difference in about a minute. And get close before you fire, closer than you'll want to. Everybody fires too early the first time; I fired at a cloud and put in a report about it.
l1_line12: He's going down. He's going down —
l1_line13: I see it. Breathe out. Wings level.
l1_line14: I didn't think he would burn.
l1_line15: They do. And you'll be quiet all the way home, which is the usual thing, so don't go worrying about that as well.
l1_line16: The second one sat behind me for half a minute. Every time I pulled, he pulled with me.
l1_line17: Because you were pulling with what you had. There's about three seconds of hard running in that engine — everything forward at once, and she comes round tighter than she's any right to. It's not for chasing a man; it's for the half second when you need to not be where his guns are.
l1_line19: Three seconds is a whole turn. Then she wants eight quiet ones — I spent mine badly at Souilly in 1915 and glided home on a hot bearing with a fitter waiting to tell me about it.
l1_line20: Three more coming up the line at you, Chardon 118. Two singles, then a pair together. Sorry — the pair is new.
l1_line21: Same as before, then, all the way to the end of it. Nothing clever. Mine's still with me.
l1_line22: The last two came in together. I lost sight of one of them behind my own wing and fired at where I thought he'd be.
l1_line25: Don't do that again for about a year. It works until the morning it doesn't, and I'd like you here for that morning.
l1_line27: Mine did for a week. They'll go on doing it on the ground for an hour yet — let them, and don't stand about where the fitters can see.
l1_line28: That's the sector clear. Bring him home, Chardon 118, and thank you both.
l1_line29: Take us in, Vasseur. I'll follow you.
l1_line31: You know where it is. You've swept it for eleven months. Fly it.
l1_after1: Six machines, two hundred and ten rounds. The armourer counted them back out of your belt and then came and found me about it.
l1_after3: It's fewer than most men spend on two. I spent four hundred on nothing at all, in the rain, in June.
l1_after4: What he's telling you is that you did well. He does it in numbers so you don't get big-headed and die of it.
l1_after6: Somebody has to translate you, Auguste.
l1_after7: Same time tomorrow. Both of you go and eat something.
